output.summary: Approved the G1001 design (attempt 3): request key as a Request-Key trailer on the immutable root commit; scan before allocating and after any failed push; one refetch-and-rescan when nothing matches and deleted goals are present (closes the same-clone fetch race found by test_design); an up-to-date create push counts as recovery; --policy-ref stays refused in cli.session before any scan (the reviewer's contrary finding was disputed with evidence and withdrawn). Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1.

responses.review_design:2:1: disputed: at 54d7e83, plugins/zzzops/zzzops/engine/cli.py:97-100 `session(args, environment=True, preview=False)` raises Refused('usage', '--policy-ref is a read-only preview ...') whenever --policy-ref is set and preview is False, before constructing a Session. cmd_new calls `s = session(a)` at cli.py:328 (no preview=True), before `s.open()` (329) and before any scan, so `new --policy-ref dev --file F` exits 1 with usage on a retry too; session.py:186-187 is a second, unreachable guard for new. The design now states this ordering explicitly in section 4 (keep session(a) ahead of the scan; do not rely on require_writable for it) and lists the test as test 10.

output.summary: Design unchanged in substance. Disputed review_design:2:1: at 54d7e83 cli.py session() (lines 97-100) refuses --policy-ref with usage for every non-preview verb before a Session exists, and cmd_new calls session(a) at line 328 before s.open() and the key scan, so a --policy-ref retry is refused before any scan. findings.text: cmd_new control flow runs the key scan before s.require_writable(), but require_writable is also where --policy-ref is refused (session.py:186-187). As written, `new --policy-ref dev --file F` for an existing request returns recovered:true (exit 0), so the already-written test_policy_ref_is_refused_even_for_a_retry (expects usage, exit 1) fails, and a read-only preview flag gets through a write verb. Fix: refuse --policy-ref with the same usage error before the scan, and defer only the write-block and engine checks until after it.

output.summary: Approved. The design now says in section 4 that this ordering must be kept, and test 10 pins it. No new material findings.

Approved. The tests cover all 10 design test items and the section 3 and 4 scan and write rules, with meaningful assertions: ids, the recovered flag, the goal_commit equal to the root, ref counts, push and fetch counts from the trace, and error code, details and hint. At c2a6bcc before implementation, 30 of the 35 new tests fail for the intended reasons. The other 5 are deliberate regression guards. The full engine suite (314 tests) shows only those 30 failures, so the fixture change breaks nothing. The threaded race outcomes are deterministic under the design. Only the path taken depends on timing, and test 9 deterministically guards the up_to_date path. No material findings.

spec:
Give each `new` request a stable identity: an optional client `request_key` in the new-goal file, defaulting to a hash of the canonical title+spec+depends_on. Record it in the goal document or as a goal-commit trailer. Before allocating an id, and after any non-ok push, scan the fetched goal tips for that key; if found, return the existing goal with `created.recovered: true` instead of allocating another id. Reject a request whose key matches a goal with different contents. Deliberately distinct goals with the same title stay allowed because the key covers the spec. Acceptance: unit tests for an exact retry, a push that lands but reports failure, concurrent identical `new` calls (one goal), a key reused with different contents (refused) and same-title distinct specs (two goals). Dropped versus the old wording: issue-based discovery, lock release and capture checkpoints (R1, R12).

title: Make `zzzops new` idempotent across retries and uncertain pushes
